newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Telstra says revenue below budget.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Telstra says revenue below budget.

text.p: Australian government-owned telecommunications group Telstra Corp on Thursday confirmed newspaper reports that revenue growth over first half to December 31 had not lived up to internal budget expectations.

"(Chief executive Frank Blount) said we are experiencing softness in areas of revenue, although that's against a fairly bullish growth projection from the budget," Telstra group manager of media relations Steve Wright told Reuters.
"It's certainly no financial crisis," he added.
Wright said Blount's comments were made to a briefing in Sydney on Wednesday.
Wright declined to elaborate on the budget forecasts for Telstra, one third of which is due for privatisation this year or next.
Newspapers on Thursday said the sluggish Australian economy, solid competition and bad debts might hobble telecommunications group Telstra's full year result.

"Telstra's long-distance call problems, a slowing economy and bad debts are believed to be threatening to slice tens of millions of dollars from this year's earnings," Melbourne's The Age newspaper reported.
The Age said Telstra sources had blamed slower than expected earnings from business customers on an economic slowdown.
Telstra chalked up a 31.5 percent rise in net profit to A$2.30 billion for the year to June 30, 1996.
The Australian Financial Review said Telstra's costs had grown four to five percent during the December half, while revenue growth was six percent, compared with an internal forecast of nine percent.
The paper also said Telstra would report a "solid" profit of about A$1.25 billion for the six months to December 31.
Telstra's Wright said no specific figures were discussed at the briefing.
"There are a number of specific details which I can't confirm," he added.
The group's net profit for the six months to December 31, 1995 was A$1.21 billion.
Wright declined to comment on whether Telstra had accrued bad debts from third party vendors of its call capacity.
The Financial Review article said it was understood Telstra had over A$400 million in bad debts that senior managers wished to provision for in the half yearly result.
